AbstractIrony and sarcastic tone in social media interactions can intensify audience attention and alter the trajectory of online discussions, especially during periods of service disruption or organizational crisis. This article examines how irony-related expressions shape engagement patterns, negative amplification, and topic drift across short-form posts. Using a text mining pipeline that combines natural language processing, sentiment-aware feature extraction, and temporal network analysis, the study compares literal complaint language with irony-laden responses in crisis conversations. Results indicate that irony-bearing messages generate stronger response cascades than neutral complaints and are more likely to broaden the discussion toward organizational accountability and recovery strategies. The findings suggest practical uses for monitoring public reaction, improving crisis response, and refining analytics systems for socially mediated reputation management.This article is categorized under:

result.title: Modeling irony-driven engagement in crisis communication on social platforms
